title: Arrangements the engine does not read — listed, never claimed

census.why: gettext is the format most worth reading and the one least readable. Without `src/extract/po.ts` the file yields `~sweep[n]` prose runs with no structure at all, so no dialect can claim what was never parsed — a row would be inert no matter how well written.

Fluent's selector syntax is a GRAMMAR, not a separator, so it needs a parser beside `icu.ts` rather than a data row. It is also the one format whose catalog rule already lists it — `**/*.ftl` is in `i18n.message-bundles` — and cannot fire, because `classify` short-circuits on sweep sites before `matchRules`.
An XML plist, and `.stringsdict` is not routed to the markup extractor. Registering the extension would give it a structural path and make it a data row, exactly as `.xcstrings` became one.
The counter-example, and the argument for the whole design: registering one extension turned an unreadable file into a dialect ROW. The engine gained an arrangement without gaining a detector.

The nastiest path in the corpus. Qt translation files use `.ts`, which this engine routes to the TypeScript grammar — so a parser is handed XML, reports unparseable regions, and the file goes down the degraded branch with `claimRatio` at 0. Nothing is lost: the sweep covers exactly the regions the grammar failed on, which is what that branch exists for.

expectations.why: LISTED, not claimed. If this ever reads `translate`, somebody wrote a `.po` extractor and this expectation must be rewritten deliberately rather than updated in passing.
The indexed form. Its number is a POSITION whose meaning lives in the `Plural-Forms:` header — a C expression the engine does not and will not evaluate.
Surfaced by the sweep, so G2 refuses to pass and the file cannot be silently skipped. That is the whole guarantee available here.
Apple's plural dictionary, surfaced and not understood.
Reached through the degraded AST branch: the TypeScript grammar failed on this region, and the sweep covered exactly what it failed on. Being accounted for at all is the claim.
CLAIMED, unlike everything else in this case, because `.xcstrings` is registered as JSON and a data row reads the resulting path. One line in an extension set and one row in a catalog.

plurals.why: A String Catalog family, read by a row rather than by a detector. `code-edit` because a new form is a nested `stringUnit` object and insertion writes a scalar sibling.
No Fluent grammar, so no family. Asserting the ABSENCE matters: a dialect that started claiming sweep runs would be reading prose fragments as forms.

knownGaps: The Symfony interval string in `src/locales/messages.en.yaml` is claimed by `vue-i18n.pipe-positional` as a three-part `zero|one|other` family. It is not one: `{0} …|]0,1] …|]1,Inf[ …` carries an explicit selector on each part, and reading them as positions mislabels all three. The `value-split` primitive has no `partSelector`, so a correct Symfony row cannot be written today — and adding an interval guard to the vue-i18n row would put Symfony knowledge inside somebody else's dialect, which is the coupling this design exists to remove.

`.stringsdict` and `.ftl` produce no plural RESIDUAL, only `unclassified` sites. The suspicion signals look for a marker in a path or a token in the text, and the sweep fragments both formats below the level where either survives. Nothing is lost — G2 still refuses to pass — but G7 cannot say 'this looks like a plural', so the dialect worklist will not mention them.

gettext's `Plural-Forms:` header is read by nothing. Even with a `.po` extractor, an index would map to a POSITION and never to a CLDR category, so such a family would be `cldr: false` and never measured for completeness. That is a smaller claim than the one made for i18next, and the true one.
